incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 4, 10, 19, 52, 53, 67, 104, 106, 155, and applicable regulations; supplemented by the Civil Code of Québec for general legal personality and the Québec Charter of the French Language for corporate-name requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), 2050 rue de Bleury, Montréal, Québec; online filing via the CLIC electronic filing system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed with the Registraire des entreprises, together with the initial registration declaration (déclaration d'immatriculation).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A Québec business corporation may be incorporated without any paid-up shares; consideration for issued shares may be cash, property, or past services. No escrow account is required for initial share capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: the directors accept and ratify the share subscription made by the incorporator for 100 common shares of the Corporation at a subscription price of CAD 0.01 per share, payment in full in cash upon issuance; FURTHER RESOLVED THAT: the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address set out in the articles, in the City of Montréal, Province of Québec, and that such address be entered in the enterprise register; FURTHER RESOLVED THAT: [Name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected, with full authority to execute banking mandates, engagement letters, and regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and French-language compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), CLIC online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name request to the Registraire for the proposed French-dominant corporate name, ensuring the name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing names in the Québec enterprise register. A numbered corporation such as '9000-0000 Québec inc.' may be used if no name is cleared. English-only names are generally refused under the Québec Charter of the French Language unless a recognized trademark exception applies.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and corporated suffix
Identification of incorporator and first directors
Request for name clearance or numbered-company election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the request may be revised with a new distinctive name or a numbered name may be selected; a clarified filing can be resubmitted without losing priority date if submitted promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and validation of articles of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of incorporation under the QBCA, specifying the authorized share structure, restrictions on share transfers (if any), first directors, and registered office address in Québec. Ensure that at least one director is a resident Canadian where less than four directors are appointed, or a majority are resident Canadians where four or more directors are appointed. No notarization is required if the incorporator signs the articles in the statutory form.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If counsel identifies drafting defects, the articles are corrected before filing; the filing is postponed only if the defect is material.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of articles and payment of filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), CLIC online filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed articles electronically through the CLIC portal or by courier to the REQ. The filing must be accompanied by the initial registration declaration and payment of the statutory fee. Electronic signature by the incorporator suffices. The registration is effective when a certificate of incorporation is issued by the Registraire.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a query or refusal, the applicant receives a written notice identifying defects; corrected documents may be refiled within the statutory response period, and a revised fee is assessed where applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certificate of incorporation and enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, download the Certificate of Incorporation and the Attestation of Registration. Verify that the enterprise number (NEQ) is active and that the registered office and director information appear correctly in the public enterprise register. Use the certificate to open bank accounts and sign contracts in the corporate name.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration data is inaccurate, file a correction declaration with the REQ; a duplicate certificate may be requested through the CLIC service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and corporate governance implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or sign a unanimous written resolution. Approve the by-laws, adopt the share subscription and issue share certificates, appoint the president, secretary and chief financial officer, approve the opening of a corporate bank account, and ratify the lease for the registered office. Record the minutes and maintain the corporate securities register and minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum is not available, the meeting is reconvened; any informal action may be ratified by a later unanimous written resolution of the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, and local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for GST/HST and QST accounts if the corporation makes or intends to make taxable supplies in Canada, and register for payroll deductions if employees are hired. Update the enterprise register with any changes and obtain any local commercial occupancy permit required by the municipality for the office. For this simulated social-casino software publisher, no real-money gaming licence from Loto-Québec or the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux is required because no cash wagering or cash payout occurs; payments are limited to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and officer designations
Identification and addresses of directors and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registrations are queried, respond through the respective online portals within the stated 30-day period with corrected supporting documents; municipal permit refusals may be cured by reapplying with lease and zoning compliance evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no factory or industrial plant is established; the activity is office-based software publishing. If a commercial office lease is occupied, the relevant municipal permit authority is the local city or arrondissement zoning and building service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial or manufacturing operating permit applies. The corporation may need only a municipal commercial occupancy certificate and, if applicable, a CNESST workplace registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-only software development and publishing do not trigger an environmental impact assessment or a certificate of authorization under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c Q-2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC process emissions, or hazardous industrial discharges are generated. Office sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer-use by-laws; electronic waste and used batteries must be managed through the applicable Québec extended producer responsibility and residual materials management programs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises must meet the fire safety requirements of the Québec Building Code and the Québec Safety Code as administered by the Régie du bâtiment du Québec; a municipal fire safety inspection may be required. Any leasehold improvements require a building permit. Occupational safety clearance and employer registrations must be completed with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for workers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; portal: My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). For Quebec QST: Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec federal/provincial business corporation, register via CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain a Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account; non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada may apply using Form RC4601-1 or through a Canadian representative. For QST, register separately with Revenu Québec using the BN (RT-2 forms) through Revenu Québec's online services or the Registraire des entreprises du Québec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box or foreign entity classification election. Available elections include: Section 216(1) election for non-resident rental income, Section 273 joint venture election (optional), and GST/HST quick method election (for eligible small businesses). Hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.4-18.6 disallow certain hybrid mismatch deductions and require income inclusion adjustments; no golden share election or similar is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) — value-added tax regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies in any calendar quarter or in the last four consecutive calendar quarters for both GST/HST and QST; non-residents subject to Canadian digital economy rules may have a different threshold, but the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold generally applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary (PEPPOL adoption in Ontario/Quebec pilots). Registrants with taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million per year must file GST/HST returns electronically. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are payment rails, not tax clearance mechanisms, and no API-based government fiscal clearance applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of electronic software or services (simulated social casino and virtual slots games) is zero-rated under Excise Tax Act Schedule VI, Part V, section 7 (services) and section 23 (intangible personal property) if the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, is not carrying on business in Canada, and the supply is not for consumption or use in Canada. Physical goods exported from Canada are zero-rated with proof of export. For digital platform sales through Apple App Store/Google Play, the app publisher must maintain records demonstrating the end-user's non-residency and that settlement occurs outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: App platform sales and royalty export reports (App Store Connect / Google Play Console) with SKU-level transaction details
Apple/Google payment settlement and payout remittance statements (gross revenue, commissions, net payment, and currency conversion)
Commercial contracts, license agreements, and end-user non-residency evidence (billing country, IP geolocation, app storefront)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess outside the normal 4-year period for misrepresentation or fraud (unlimited assessment period). For knowingly or negligently making false statements, gross negligence penalties under Excise Tax Act section 285.1 apply at 25% of the tax that would have been understated or overclaimed. Improperly claimed export zero-rating is reversed (clawback) and tax is assessed at the applicable GST/HST and QST rates (combined 14.975% in Quebec), plus arrears interest (currently 5% per annum statutory rate) and administrative penalties. CRA increasingly uses platform payment data from Apple/Google to cross-check zero-rated digital exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the monetary authority; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as the federal prudential regulator of deposit-taking institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as the AML/CFT supervisor; and the Minister of Finance for residual authority under the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada operates a freely floating exchange-rate regime with no discrete foreign-exchange control statute or foreign exchange administration certificate requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility. Canada is a signatory to the OECD Codes of Liberalisation; there are no capital controls, no approval or registration gate for foreign direct investment into a Quebec Business Corporation, and no restriction on profit repatriation by non-resident shareholders. Dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees may be remitted freely, subject to federal Part XIII withholding tax (general 25%, treaty-reduced as applicable, e.g., 5/15% dividends under the Canada-US DTA) and provincial withholding on certain payments made to non-residents (Quebec levy analogous to Part XIII). A non-resident-owned Quebec corporation is not subject to branch tax unless it carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada via an unincorporated form. Compliance watchpoints: aggregate inbound transaction value must be screened against the Investment Canada Act (non-reviewable below the 2025 WTO enterprise-value threshold of approximately CAD 1.3 billion for WTO-treaty investors); and all cross-border electronic funds transfers must be reported to FINTRAC by the bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline for conversion or repatriation of export proceeds, no mandatory surrender ratio, and no requirement that export receipts be converted to Canadian dollars. Exporters may retain income in any freely usable currency. The only binding obligations are reporting-related: (i) the depository bank must report cross-border SWIFT EFTs to FINTRAC (all SWIFT-originated cross-border transfers, no de minimis threshold, whereas non-SWIFT transfers above CAD 10,000 are reportable); (ii) physical cross-border currency movements of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable under the PCMLTFA; and (iii) Statistics Canada / Bank of Canada balance-of-payments surveys may require periodic disclosure of large transactions. The Quebec corporation may therefore hold USD/EUR balances in its operating account or in linked foreign-currency clearing accounts without fiscal penalty.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. Canada does not belong to the EU/UK electronic money institution (EMI) passporting regime; an offshore EMI licence confers no authorization to offer deposit-taking or payment services in Canada absent compliance with the Bank Act and the PCMLTFA. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or EMI-as-a-service platforms) may be used only as narrow treasury utilities for vendor disbursements, payroll, and currency conversion, and only after the EMI registers with FINTRAC as a foreign money services business (MSB) where it has a Canadian nexus or solicits Canadian clients. A Quebec Business Corporation may legally maintain an offshore EMI account for operational float, but capital escrow, settlement, and blockchain treasury-grade liquidity must remain in a Canadian Schedule I bank because the EMI channel cannot provide deposit insurance (CDIC), LVTS settlement, or regulated correspondent clearing. Recommendation: use a Canadian-licensed bank as the primary clearing account and a FINTRAC-registered fintech (e.g., Wise for cross-border FX) as a secondary, capped-flow corridor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Conditional remote opening is permitted, but a physical or live-video interview is de facto mandatory for a Medium-Risk-Enhanced social-casino entity. Under FINTRAC identification rules, a corporation must be identified through a certified true copy of its certificate of incorporation, articles, register of directors, and the enterprise-specific identification from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (NEQ) — not solely through a remote selfie. Non-resident directors and beneficial owners holding more than 25% of shares must generally complete a '100-point' credential check; banks in practice require (i) a recorded video call for each ultimate shareholder above the 25% threshold and at least one signing officer, and (ii) a notarized account resolution — or a wet-ink board resolution with a recognized Quebec resident signatory — before the mandate is activated. RBC and National Bank permit fully remote onboarding for domestic, arms-length directors with e-signatures, but the presence of a Canadian resident director or a registered Quebec agent for service (acting as mandate holder) materially accelerates approval. For enhanced-due-diligence segments, Scotiabank historically requires an in-branch signature at a Montreal or Toronto commercial banking centre.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Social-casino in-app purchase flow (Apple IAP / Google Play Billing) creates a pattern of high-volume micro-transactions, interpreted by transaction-monitoring engines as structured deposits or potential money-laundering layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant of Record agreements with Apple and Google; SOC 1/SOC 2 reports from the app store platforms; ISO 20022 / MT940 historical transaction export demonstrating average ticket size < USD 20 and refund ratio < 2%; FINTRAC-compliant written AML/ATF policy with automated transaction monitoring and unusual-transaction escalation workflow; signed attestation that virtual chips have no cash-out, exchange, or transfer value.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mischaracterization of simulated slots as real-money gambling, triggering prohibitions under the Criminal Code (Canada) s.197-204 and Quebec's R.S.Q. c. R-6.2 (Lotteries, Gaming, Betting, Casino and Amusement Machine Act).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion issued by a Quebec-licensed gaming lawyer confirming the absence of the 'consideration-prize-chance' tripartite test; determinism certificate from a licensed game-testing laboratory (e.g., GLI) proving no real monetary payout; geo-blocking configuration report restricting access in Canadian gambling-restricted contexts; full terms-of-service and end-user licence agreement prohibiting secondary-market virtual chip trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident foreign parent or overseas beneficial owner injecting capital increases source-of-funds and politically exposed person (PEP) risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registry extracts for the ultimate parent (corporate registrar or equivalent); Canada-compatible register of individuals with significant control (ISC) for the Quebec corporation; source-of-wealth statement with six months of bank statements of the funding shareholder; bank reference letter from the parent's home-country institution; notarized passports and valid proof of address for all UBOs above 10% beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative screening hits on sanctions lists or adverse media linked to the gaming sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time and retroactive sanctions/placement screening output covering UN, OFAC, EU, and Canada's Autonomous Sanctions List; adverse-media search with Boolean 'social casino / slots / lottery' filters; written board representation confirming no real-money gambling licence and no connection to blacklisted payment processors; audited financial statements of the corporate group and detailed intercompany transfer-pricing documentation under s.247 of the Income Tax Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: the non-resident shareholder or affiliate initiates a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank through its correspondent to the designated Canadian Schedule I bank in Montreal. Recommended field mapping: field 50K (Ordering Customer) must name the actual funding entity; field 56A (Intermediary) is the Canadian bank's US correspondent for USD (e.g., JPMorgan or Citi New York); field 57A (Beneficiary Bank) is the Quebec branch of the Schedule I bank; field 59 (Beneficiary) is the Quebec corporation's escrow or operating account with the NEQ number and registered address; field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION / CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — INVOICE/REF [X]'. To satisfy KYC, the bank will require a board resolution authorizing the share issuance, the updated ISC register, and a source-of-funds declaration. Funds are not usable until cleared (typically T+1 for CAD/USD, T+2 for EUR/GBP) and the bank will file FINTRAC EFT reports on the inbound leg. If capital injection is a subscription for newly issued shares, the proceeds must be credited to an escrowed 'Capital Subscription' sub-account until the articles of amendment or share certificate record is updated; for a loan contribution, an intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest must support the credit. Aggregate transaction review under the Investment Canada Act applies only above the WTO enterprise-value threshold; for the typical simulation-company capital round (CAD 1-50M) a post-closing ISED notification may be required if the investing entity is foreign-controlled.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails available to the Quebec social-casino operator: (1) SWIFT MT103 for international wire disbursements to overseas licensors, game studios, and influencer agencies — required for EUR/GBP/SEK vendor payments and for USD payments when a US clearing branch is not used; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) for significant one-off licensing fees or platform technology acquisitions — the issuing Canadian bank will require 100% collateralization for the embedded credit line of a new entity; (3) Canadian domestic Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR) payment orders for local payroll and Quebec tax remittances; (4) ACSS EFT credit for same-bank and ACH-style domestic bulk payments (e.g., refunds, merchant payouts); (5) a dedicated USD clearing sub-account with the bank's US correspondent to receive Apple/Google remittances and make US vendor payments via Fedwire/CHIPS without a double conversion. Outbound transfers of CAD 10,000+ via non-SWIFT rail must be reported to FINTRAC; SWIFT rail is inherently reportable by the bank. Recommended treasury policy: maintain a primary CAD account, one USD concentration account, and a capped EUR transit account; clear all app-store payout settlements via SWIFT MT103 from the merchant-of-record agreement remittance schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forward (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) under the ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Option Definitions with a Canadian Schedule I bank — most liquid for hedging forecast USD revenue from Apple/Google.
FX swap (simultaneous spot and forward exchange) for short-term funding of USD-denominated intercompany liabilities.
Cross-currency swap (CCS) for matching long-term CAD-denominated operating expenses against USD-denominated app-store revenue streams.
Vanilla over-the-counter foreign currency option (call/put) to hedge budget-rate exposure on fixed licensing fees.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) — permissible in Canada only as a residual instrument where the counterparty cannot physically deliver CAD; in Canada’s fully convertible regime, a deliverable forward is the standard and NDFs are unnecessary; if an offshore bank executes an NDF, the transaction remains reportable under provincial OTC derivative trade-reporting rules and subject to OSFI margin requirements where the Canadian entity is a financial end-user.
Total return swap or synthetic CAD/USD forward overlay — permitted for sophisticated corporate users but subject to the provincial derivatives framework and bilateral trade documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 200 late-filing penalty; failure to file for three consecutive years permits Corporations Canada to issue a Notice of Intent to Dissolve and administratively dissolve the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Update Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour annuelle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the registration anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 26 late-filing surcharge; default extending more than one year past the anniversary may trigger administrative strike-off (dissolution) by the REQ, terminating the enterprise's legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual attestation of the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (attestation integrated in the annual declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual declaration; any share transfer changing significant control must be entered in the register within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted annual confirmation constitutes an offence punishable by fines up to CAD 15,000 for the corporation and CAD 5,000 for directors or officers; register inaccuracy also exposes the corporation to administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) and annual resolutions of directors and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate minutes and statutory minute book (no external government filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once per calendar year with intervals between AGMs not exceeding 15 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be held personally liable for failing to convene the AGM; non-compliance with minute book upkeep may undermine limited liability under the corporate veil doctrine, though no government penalty is assessed.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: For a corporation carrying on business in Quebec through a permanent establishment, the general combined rate is ordinarily 26.5%: 15% federal plus 11.5% Quebec. A qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) may generally access a combined 12.2% rate on eligible active business income within the applicable federal and Quebec business limits: 9% federal plus 3.2% Quebec. Eligibility, business limits, associated-corporation rules, taxable-capital limits, and income-type restrictions apply.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible CCPCs may claim the federal small business deduction and Quebec small business deduction, subject to separate eligibility and phase-out rules. Federal and Quebec research and development incentives may apply to qualifying expenditures; Quebec also provides other targeted credits subject to their statutory conditions. No gaming-specific corporate income tax holiday is identified for simulated social-casino game publishing. App-store distribution, virtual currency, prizes, cash-out functionality, and the actual game mechanics may affect regulatory and tax characterization.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA-certified software or an authorized electronic filing service. Quebec: CO-17, Déclaration de revenus des sociétés, filed electronically with Revenu Québec using an authorized method. Separate federal and Quebec returns are generally required where the corporation has a Quebec filing obligation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax returns; federal and Quebec instalments may be required monthly or quarterly, depending on the corporation's status and applicable rules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The federal T2 and Quebec CO-17 are generally due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Tax balances are generally due two months after year-end; a qualifying CCPC meeting the statutory conditions may have three months to pay the federal balance and may qualify for corresponding Quebec payment relief. Instalment due dates apply separately. Confirm the applicable rules for the corporation's taxation year and status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the legal name, business number, taxation-year start and end dates, address, province or territory of permanent establishments, and applicable corporation identifiers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or otherwise subject to Canadian filing requirements must use its Canadian business number and report its Canadian tax year and relevant Canadian presence. A non-resident shareholder does not itself make a Canadian-incorporated subsidiary a non-resident corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 9 and related ownership information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report shareholder and control information required by the return and schedules, including CCPC status where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign ownership and control accurately. A corporation controlled, directly or indirectly, by non-residents generally is not a CCPC and cannot claim the federal small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting net income or loss to income or loss for income tax purposes, including non-deductible expenses, tax depreciation, reserves, and other tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income attributable to Canadian business activities and apply the applicable Canadian-source and treaty rules. Maintain support for deductions, allocations, and foreign-currency conversions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report capital cost allowance classes, additions, dispositions, recapture, terminal losses, and tax depreciation claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Canadian tax depreciation for property relevant to the Canadian tax computation; accounting depreciation is not a substitute for the statutory calculation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 23 and small-business deduction claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide associated-corporation and business-limit information where required and calculate the federal small business deduction if eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-controlled corporation is generally ineligible for the CCPC deduction. Identify associated corporations and allocate the business limit as required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 50 and Schedule 200 balance and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report significant shareholders where required and calculate federal taxable income, tax, credits, instalments, and balance owing or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report relevant ownership accurately and do not treat treaty relief from withholding as an exemption from the corporation's own Canadian filing or tax obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report Quebec identification information, taxation year, Quebec establishment or allocation information, taxable income, deductions, credits, tax payable, and instalments using the current CO-17 and applicable schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A corporation with a Quebec filing obligation must report Quebec-attributable income under the applicable allocation rules. Foreign ownership does not by itself remove a Quebec filing obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal and Quebec late-filing penalties generally include an initial percentage of unpaid tax plus an additional monthly percentage, subject to statutory maximums; enhanced penalties may apply to repeat failures or gross negligence. Interest on unpaid tax and instalments accrues under the applicable prescribed-rate rules. The ordinary federal late-filing penalty is generally 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month late, up to 12 months; higher repeat-failure penalties may apply. Quebec has its own penalty and interest provisions. There is no general daily late-filing surcharge. Exact liability depends on the return, filing history, tax owing, and applicable statutory provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Part XIII withholding tax is generally 25% on dividends paid or credited by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident, subject to a tax treaty or other statutory relief. Treaty rates vary by recipient residence, beneficial ownership, and shareholding; many treaties provide a reduced rate for qualifying corporate direct-investment dividends and a higher rate for portfolio dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before applying a reduced treaty rate, the Canadian payer should obtain and retain appropriate evidence that the recipient is the beneficial owner and resident of a treaty jurisdiction, normally including a valid certificate of residence or tax residence certificate and prescribed declarations or forms, such as NR301, NR302, or NR303 as applicable. The payer must assess limitation-on-benefits, anti-conduit, principal-purpose, and other treaty requirements, withhold and remit the correct amount, and report payments on the required information returns, including NR4 where applicable. Treaty relief is not automatic; uncertainty may require a CRA ruling or other professional review. Quebec-source withholding and reporting obligations must also be assessed separately.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Part XIII rate is generally 25% on royalties paid or credited to a non-resident. Treaty royalty rates vary by treaty and royalty category and may be reduced, including to zero in some treaties. Canadian withholding tax generally does not apply to ordinary interest paid to an arm's-length non-resident lender, subject to statutory exceptions; interest paid to a non-arm's-length non-resident is generally subject to 25% withholding unless reduced or exempt under a treaty or statutory rule. Treaty interest rates vary. Classify payments by their legal and economic substance; software, copyright, platform, and distribution payments may be royalties, business profits, or another category depending on the rights granted.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada does not impose a general OECD-style Master File and Local File filing threshold. Under Income Tax Act section 247, contemporaneous documentation is required for relevant non-arm's-length transactions with non-residents and must generally be provided within three months after a written request. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational enterprise groups with consolidated group revenue of at least CAD 1 billion, subject to statutory filing rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no general regime named Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Canadian transfer-pricing, treaty anti-abuse, general anti-avoidance, sham, beneficial-ownership, and business-purpose doctrines may nevertheless apply. Maintain evidence of decision-making, personnel, functions, assets, risks, contractual rights, and actual conduct, especially for intellectual property ownership, intercompany services, financing, and royalty arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion, false statements, or wilful failure to comply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly making false or deceptive tax statements, destroying or falsifying records, wilfully evading tax, or participating in an arrangement intended to conceal taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239 provides for criminal fines and imprisonment. On summary conviction, the fine may generally range from 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, with imprisonment up to two years; indictable prosecution can carry imprisonment up to five years. Other penalties, interest, reassessments, and provincial consequences may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for corporate income tax solely because they are directors. Personal criminal liability may arise from their own participation, authorization, or legally attributable conduct. Separate statutory director-liability rules can apply to specified remittances and other obligations. Civil recovery, prosecution, and travel restrictions require applicable legal authority and process; they are not automatic consequences of a tax assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to use arm's-length terms for non-arm's-length cross-border transactions, failure to maintain or provide required contemporaneous documentation, or failure to report transactions accurately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 247 permits transfer-pricing adjustments. A penalty may apply where the net transfer-pricing adjustment exceeds the statutory threshold, generally the greater of CAD 5 million and 10% of gross revenue, and the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts to determine and use arm's-length amounts. The penalty is generally 10% of the relevant net adjustment; interest and consequential reassessments may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The adjustment and penalty are generally imposed on the corporation. Directors may face personal exposure for their own knowing participation in an offence or under a separate statutory liability provision; ordinary director status alone does not establish personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late filing, late payment, or deficient records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the T2 or CO-17 by its statutory deadline, failure to pay tax or instalments when due, or failure to maintain and provide adequate books and records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties, arrears and instalment interest, reassessments, and possible prosecution for wilful non-compliance may apply under federal or Quebec law. Penalties depend on the return, filing history, tax owing, and conduct; no single daily surcharge applies generally.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate tax and filing liabilities ordinarily remain corporate liabilities. Personal liability may arise under specific statutory provisions or from a director's own offence, not merely from holding office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper treaty claims or withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a reduced treaty withholding rate without establishing residence, beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, or required supporting evidence; failing to withhold, remit, or report tax on payments to non-residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unremitted withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Treaty benefits may be denied under treaty terms or domestic anti-avoidance rules. Separate reporting penalties may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically personally liable for corporate withholding-tax assessments. Statutory director-liability provisions may apply to specified unremitted amounts, subject to their conditions and available defences; personal criminal liability requires the applicable offence and proof.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed gambling or misleading game monetization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Adding cash prizes, cash-out, transferable value, or other features that cause a simulated social-casino product to fall within gambling or lottery regulation without the required authorization; misrepresenting odds, purchases, or virtual-currency value to consumers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The absence of a stated statutory licence requirement for the described simulation does not establish that every implementation is exempt. Criminal Code gambling provisions, provincial gaming laws, consumer-protection rules, platform policies, and payment-provider requirements may apply depending on game mechanics and monetization. Penalties are offence- and jurisdiction-specific; obtain a Quebec gaming-law assessment before launch or feature changes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate status does not protect individuals from liability for their own participation in an offence or from applicable officer or director liability provisions. Civil, administrative, and criminal consequences depend on the conduct and governing law; travel bans or imprisonment are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company, sham, or artificial intellectual-property arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a corporation with no genuine functions or decision-making to claim treaty benefits, shift profits, or receive royalties unsupported by actual ownership, control, personnel, or risk-bearing activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible outcomes include denial of treaty benefits, transfer-pricing adjustments, application of the general anti-avoidance rule or other anti-avoidance provisions, withholding-tax assessments, interest, penalties, and reassessment. A shell structure alone is not a standalone offence; sanctions require the applicable statutory basis and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate separateness is not automatically disregarded. Directors may face personal exposure for their own misconduct, statutory liabilities, or participation in an offence. Civil restitution, travel restrictions, and imprisonment require separate legal grounds and due process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly facilitating transactions involving criminal proceeds, concealing beneficial ownership, or failing to comply with applicable reporting or recordkeeping obligations where the business is a reporting entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Whether a game publisher or payment intermediary is a reporting entity under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act depends on its activities and statutory status. Criminal laundering offences can carry severe fines and imprisonment; reporting and recordkeeping penalties apply only where the relevant statutory duties attach. Assess Apple and Google payment flows, third-party processors, cash-out features, and any direct financial services separately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals may be liable for their own knowing participation or for offences established under applicable law. Director status alone does not create automatic criminal liability; civil recovery, travel restrictions, and imprisonment require legal authority and process.
